- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is trending up, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent price spike (last 3–5 days) is followed by forecast overshoot, cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.  
- When sentiment is positive (especially > 0.3) and forecast is trending down, adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to avoid mean reversion bias.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently higher than forecast (especially after 10–15 days), add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next period.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly negative and forecast is flat, slightly increase forecast to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves when sentiment is positive — model tends to underreact to bullish sentiment.
